hypotheses.H1_gemv_unroll: REFUTED on sm_120. AMD gemv-autotune (46dccd6) does not transfer: decode object is already occ-1 (174 regs=1 block/SM), and it allocates for the union of all decode arms, so deepening GV_UNROLL 8->16 raised whole-kernel regs 174->204->240 (0 spill) yet regressed decode +0.9% at 1k/16k (starved flash-decode/norms). Kept UN=8, no kernel change.
hypotheses.H2_flash_nsplit: WON, shipped. 188-SM CU-fill formula gives ns12 (1.0x flash fill) for the 32-head 31B; ns16 (1.36x oversubscribe) beats ns12 at EVERY ctx (bf16 -0.2%@1k .. -5.8%@128k; fp8 -8.6%@128k). ns24 over-splits (worse than ns16).
hypotheses.H3_fixed_intercept: MEASURED. LSQ tpot=a+b*ctx: plow ns12 a=47.51 b=127.2ms/1k-ctx; plow ns16 a=47.40 b=99.2; vLLM a=45.38 b=81.1. ns16 cuts the KV slope -22% (near vLLM's 81) but not the intercept; plow's ~47.4ms fixed per-token cost vs vLLM 45.4 = +2.0ms 60-layer dispatch floor. Reported, not redesigned (per task).

verdict_decode_wins: NO. bf16 decode still trails vLLM +3.2..8.9% (was +5.4..15.5%). ns16 roughly halves the long-ctx gap and is greedy-token-identical, but 31B does NOT win like the 12B; the residual is the fixed ~2.0ms 60-layer dispatch intercept plus a shared bf16-KV flash floor.

parity.bf16_ns16_vs_ns12: byte-identical greedy tokens at 32k AND 128k -> ns16 is greedy-equivalent to the P2 default (ns12) which PASSED the HF set (p2 48/48, p3 31/31 incl. >1024-window-crossing, p1 reconverging near-tie). Parity INHERITED, PASS.
parity.device_vs_host_argmax: AGREE at every ctx (1k..128k), bf16 and fp8, ns16.
parity.fp8_vs_bf16: identical generated tokens at 16k/32k/64k/128k; 4k differs at 3/129 near-ties — matches the P2 fp8 agreement pattern. PASS.
parity.oracle: interp kernels byte-identical to HEAD (no kernel change); sm_120 interp-op oracle unaffected.

campaigns.config: SHIPPED nsplit=16 (default after the emitter change). methodology: prompt of length=ctx primed via PREFILL, then 128 decode tokens; discard 16 warmup, report over 112 timed steps.

campaigns.note: H2 A/B. ns12=old default, ns16=shipped, ns24=over-split. ns16 wins at every ctx; ns24 worse than ns16.
H1 REFUTED. Deeper decode GEMV unroll regresses on sm_120 (already occ-1). regs: UN8=174, UN16=204, UN16/GLU8=240 (all 0-spill).

campaigns.methodology: chunked prefill of an N-token prompt (buckets to 8192), wall time from first launch to first generated token. nsplit-independent. vs vLLM served TTFT (includes 1st decode token). T5 cp.async KV-stream flash-prefill + T4 mma P-V kernels.

campaigns.config: SHIPPED nsplit=16. weight-only w8a16, per-output-channel e4m3 (amax/448); 410 projections (60 layers x 7). Twins model.safetensors 29.30 GB. DECODE GEMV_FP8/GEMV_GLU_FP8; prefill uses T6 fp8 GEMM (w8a16).
campaigns.unblocked: T6 slim fp8 pkt (3be7888) elides the dead bf16 prefill projections -> fp8 weights 29.9 GiB (was 84.5 with bf16 prefill twins), so the FULL ladder 1k->128k now fits (55.2 GiB at 128k). P2 was OOM-blocked above ~4.6k.

campaigns.verdict: Closes the long-ctx gap (128k +5.4%->+2.0%, 64k tie, 32k WIN -1.1%) at a small short-ctx cost (1k +0.4% vs base). Does NOT flip 31B to a win at EVERY ctx: decode GEMV bodies are HBM-bound and already = vLLM (trace), and the interpreter dispatch floor is 0.66 ms (skeleton). The full-layer flash imbalance was the fixable residual and this takes it.
campaigns.parity: greedy tokens ns47 == base at 32k and 128k (nsplit is an exact online-softmax reduction reorder); oracle inherited-green (emitter-only, no kernel change).
